updates.headline: Introducing the Built Environment AI Governance Intelligence Series
updates.summary: A recurring, source-backed briefing on how AI governance is starting to shape professional obligations, buyer decisions and commercial outcomes across the built environment.
body: The series follows one question: how is AI governance beginning to affect professional obligations, buyer decisions and commercial outcomes in the built environment?

It runs in three layers. The Governance Pulse is a seven-slide LinkedIn briefing every 14 days on what genuinely moved. The Governance Monitor follows monthly and explains whether isolated developments form a pattern. A quarterly State of AI Governance report brings comparable periods together, with its method and limitations open to inspection.
Every public conclusion traces back to a dated source. Tender observations are reported with their sample and denominator, and corrections are recorded rather than quietly replaced.

The comparison point for the series is 29 September 2026. It starts from the RICS professional standard on the responsible use of AI in surveying practice, the Cabinet Office's PPN 017 on transparency of AI use in procurement, and ISO/IEC 42001.

updates.headline: FNX Governance Platform reaches v1
updates.summary: The platform helps organisations move beyond a folder of AI policy documents to a connected governance system.
body: Feenix has reached v1 status for the FNX Governance Platform, helping organisations move beyond standalone AI policy documents to a structured governance system.
Aligned with RICS, ISO/IEC 42001 and EU AI Act principles, the platform supports responsible AI adoption through connected policies, risk management, evidence and oversight.

updates.headline: The Compliance Cost Gap: what the RICS AI standard costs UK surveyors
updates.summary: A transparent model of year-one, sector-wide compliance costs under the RICS standard on the responsible use of AI, and who carries the burden.
body: What does the RICS standard on the responsible use of AI actually cost UK surveyors? Feenix built a transparent model to find out.
The model estimates around GBP 39 million in year-one sector-wide compliance costs. It also shows that firms reporting no AI adoption still carry baseline costs.

updates.headline: Feenix introduces its founding partner ecosystem
updates.summary: Four partners covering the full lifecycle of responsible AI adoption in the built environment: governance, implementation, technical grounding and delivery.
body: Feenix has introduced its founding partner ecosystem: four deliberate relationships covering the full lifecycle of responsible AI adoption in the built environment.

Clearnorth (known across the sector as The QS People) connects responsible AI initiatives with organisations exploring how AI can support their business. Serpin brings experience governing and deploying AI within large, complex organisations. Built Intelligence provides technical expertise grounded in the systems used across the built environment. Vidos supports delivery, helping teams turn responsible AI into something they can adopt and sustain.
Responsible AI adoption is not a single-vendor problem. The ecosystem brings governance, implementation, technical grounding and practical delivery together.

updates.headline: Feenix confirmed as RICS Tech Partner and IAPP member
updates.summary: Two memberships that ground Feenix's governance tools in recognised professional and regulatory standards.
body: Feenix has been confirmed as a Tech Partner of the Royal Institution of Chartered Surveyors, aligning its development to the standards RICS members and regulated firms are required to follow.

Feenix is also now a member of the International Association of Privacy Professionals, so its governance frameworks draw on established international practice in AI accountability, privacy and data governance.

updates.headline: Feenix launches publicly and introduces the Feenix Braintrust
updates.summary: An inaugural launch dinner marked Feenix's public launch and introduced five independent advisers whose role is to challenge Feenix, not endorse it.
body: Feenix held its inaugural launch dinner in June 2026, bringing together founding partners, Braintrust members and sector leaders. It marked Feenix's public launch and the formal introduction of the partner ecosystem and advisory board.

The Feenix Braintrust brings together five independent advisers: Davin Dhillon (Strategy and Growth), Danielle Lodge (Enterprise Operations), Scott Druck (AI Implementation), Kate Vandermark (Communications) and Marcia Weekes-Spears (People and Organisational Change).
An organisation that builds governance tools for others should be able to show governance in how it operates. The Braintrust is part of that.
